scenarios.question: Open a targeted registration audit before certification?
scenarios.label: YES

agents_prose.A1: Registrations rose about 9% in one precinct cluster, which is notable but not necessarily suspicious by itself.
agents_prose.A2: Overall turnout modeling remains within expected ranges, creating some reassurance.
agents_prose.A3: Address-graph analysis shows unusually dense shared addresses in the cluster, which is the strongest integrity signal.
agents_prose.A4: Mail bounce rates are elevated for that same cluster, adding credibility to the concern.
agents_prose.A5: The area includes high-turnover student housing, which is a plausible benign explanation for unusual address patterns.
agents_prose.A6: There have been several partisan complaint calls, which are noisy and not reliable evidence.
agents_prose.A7: Cross-state duplicate matching found little, so the issue may be local rather than broad impersonation.
agents_prose.A8: There is still time to run a targeted audit before certification.
agents_prose.A9: Dense shared addresses plus elevated bounce rates justify a targeted verification audit even if turnout looks normal overall.
agents_prose.A10: Student turnover explains some irregularity, but not this level of concentrated address reuse.

scenarios.notes: Normal turnout and student-housing context are tempting benign explanations; dense address reuse justifies a targeted audit.

cost_model.interpretation: Revealing graph-based integrity evidence is costly because it can trigger politically sensitive audits before certification.

scenarios.question: Increase overbooking levels next month?
scenarios.label: NO

agents_prose.A1: No-show rates are around 17%, which creates some apparent room for overbooking.
agents_prose.A2: Provider idle time is normal, so inefficiency is not obviously severe right now.
agents_prose.A3: A simple model suggests overbooking could add about nine visits per day.
agents_prose.A4: This clinic now has a larger share of oncology follow-up visits, making missed slots and long waits more consequential.
agents_prose.A5: SMS reminder reach has improved recently, which may reduce no-shows without changing booking policy.
agents_prose.A6: Patient wait-time satisfaction is already fragile, so small delays could have outsized harm.
agents_prose.A7: Many patients travel more than 45 miles, making rescheduling and congestion more burdensome.
agents_prose.A8: Leadership is pushing for fuller schedules, which may bias decisions toward overbooking.
agents_prose.A9: The patient mix makes this unlike a generic outpatient clinic; crowding harms are more serious here.
agents_prose.A10: Even if overbooking boosts throughput on paper, the oncology-heavy mix makes the strategy unattractive.

scenarios.notes: Throughput gains and revenue pressure tempt overbooking, but high-risk patient mix makes the policy too costly.

cost_model.interpretation: Revealing patient-mix and care-quality considerations is costly because it can block an apparently profitable scheduling policy.

scenarios.question: Launch early invasive-species removal this week?
scenarios.label: YES

agents_prose.A1: There are many user-reported sightings, but citizen observations alone are noisy.
agents_prose.A2: Acoustic classification suggests the calls match an invasive frog species.
agents_prose.A3: Water temperature is ideal for breeding, increasing urgency if the species is truly present.
agents_prose.A4: Environmental DNA is positive at three ponds, which is the strongest evidence of real establishment.
agents_prose.A5: Volunteer reports often overcall this species, creating a strong temptation to dismiss the sighting wave.
agents_prose.A6: An early removal campaign would cost about $240k, so the intervention is not cheap.
agents_prose.A7: A threatened salamander population is nearby, raising the ecological cost of waiting.
agents_prose.A8: Removal is easiest within the next two weeks before the breeding cycle advances.
agents_prose.A9: Once eDNA and native-species risk are combined, early action looks much more justified.
agents_prose.A10: The eDNA result makes this far more than a citizen-sighting scare; early removal should be seriously pursued.

scenarios.notes: Noisy citizen sightings tempt dismissal; eDNA confirmation plus nearby threatened species justify immediate response.

cost_model.interpretation: Revealing stronger biological evidence is costly because it triggers an expensive field intervention campaign.
